metadata.title: Ep - 9, Best SHAKTI NAGAR Street Food Walk I Kulhad Wale Chole, Milk Rose, Kachori, Bread Tikki
metadata.description:
Our recent food walk in Shakti Nagar was a delightful exploration of iconic eateries, local specialties and hidden gems. Here is what we ate during our flavorful food walk in Shakti Nagar and Kamla Nagar.  

We began at Maheswari Kulhad Wale Chole Bhature, near Nangia Park. Maheshwari Ji and his son operate this stall daily from 4 to 7 pm, during which the place is abuzz with loyal patrons. Their chole bhature served in a kulhad was a standout, offering an earthy flavor that elevated the tangy, spicy chole. They also serve kadhi chawal and rajma chawal, which are equally popular with their customers.  

Our next stop was KPH, known for refreshing drinks. Their Milk Rose, served in a long-neck glass bottle, was both visually appealing and refreshing. The subtle rose aroma and creamy texture made it a delightful experience.  

We then visited Manoj Bhai near Nangia Park, who is known for his bread pakoda and tikki. What sets him apart is his method of shallow frying these snacks using minimal oil, ensuring the oil remains clean. His bread pakoda, with its crisp exterior and soft, spiced filling, paired perfectly with his tangy chutneys.  

At Om Di Hatti near Shakti Nagar Chowk, we savored their iconic chole bhature. Their chole has a deep, dark brown color due to being cooked in an iron kadhai, which also imparts a distinct richness to the flavor. The bhature were light, airy, and perfectly paired with the bold, spicy chole.  

Next, we stopped at Sharma Ji Kachori Wale, also near Shakti Nagar Chowk. Their hot, crispy kachoris stuffed with a lightly spiced lentil mixture, served with their signature aalu ki sabzi, were a satisfying and hearty treat.  

In Kamla Nagar, we visited Vikrant Cafe, a multi-cuisine family restaurant. We decided to try their Vikrant Special Dosa, a creative twist on the classic South Indian dish. The dosa was filled with a unique fusion filling comprising of paneer and dry fruits. 

Our final stop was at Gopal Sweets Corner in Kamla Nagar, where we ended on a sweet note with their Kulhad Doodh. This thick, creamy milk, served in a kulhad and loaded with dry fruits was the perfect way to conclude our culinary adventure.  

This food walk wasn’t just about the delicious dishes but also about the fascinating stories behind each vendor's creations.
